Revised assessment incorporating FSR insights:
- Economic tone: “continued to expand at a solid pace” is positive; labor market easing but still tight and inflation moderating, which supports a cautiously upbeat read on growth.
- Policy stance: Holding 5.25–5.50% and stressing “greater confidence” before cuts plus continued balance-sheet reduction is hawkish and implies “higher-for-longer,” tempering the positive growth signal.
- FSR lens (financial stability): The FSR highlights persistent vulnerabilities—elevated asset valuations, higher long-term rates, potential Treasury market liquidity strains in stress, CRE pressures (notably via CMBS), leverage buildup, nonbank funding risks, and fiscal debt sustainability/foreign divestment concerns. These elevate downside tail risks and further mute any dovish read.
- Offsets in the FSR: Bank funding pressures eased by late 2023; BTFP wound down in March 2024; some securitization markets recovered. These improvements prevent a negative read but don’t erase the vulnerabilities.

Net: Slightly positive economic tone, moderated by hawkish policy and lingering financial stability risks flagged in the FSR.
